info.title: Flashduty Open API
info.description: Public HTTP API for the Flashduty incident management platform — incidents, notification templates, channels, schedules, monitors, RUM, and platform administration. Every operation is authenticated with an `app_key` query parameter issued from the Flashduty console under Account → APP Keys. Responses follow a uniform envelope: `{ request_id, data }` on success, `{ request_id, error }` on failure.

## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **200 requests/day**; **100 requests/minute**; **10 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | None — any valid `app_key` can call this operation |

## Usage

- The response is a `text/csv` stream delivered with `Content-Disposition: attachment` — it is not wrapped in the standard envelope. The filename is `rum-issues-<timestamp>.csv`, stamped in the requested `time_zone`. Read `X-Export-Total` and `X-Export-Truncated` response headers instead of a body field.
- The export reads the first 100 matching rows (`ExportMaxRows`); `X-Export-Truncated` is `true` when more issues match. `p` and `limit` are ignored.
- The request filters are exactly those of `POST /rum/issue/list` — an export is "what I am looking at, as a file".
- `export_fields` names the CSV columns in the order they appear. Unknown keys are rejected with a parameter error; an empty array uses the default column set.
- `time_zone` must be a valid IANA zone name (e.g. `Asia/Shanghai`, `UTC`); timestamps are rendered in that zone and time columns carry the zone in their header. Invalid names are rejected.
- `console_origin` is used to build the `issue_url` column; the service cannot infer it (SaaS, on-premises and dev releases answer on different origins).
- Every call is recorded in the account's audit log with the caller's member ID, request payload, and resulting error (if any). Do not put secrets in request fields.

200.description: Success. CSV attachment, not a JSON envelope.

X-Export-Total.description: Total number of issues matching the filters, before the row cap.

X-Export-Truncated.description: `true` when more issues matched than the 100-row cap and the file was truncated.

schema.description: CSV file content. The header row matches the exported columns in order; values are sanitized against spreadsheet formula injection.

- `rules` items carry the full internal row (including `account_id`, `created_by`, `id`, `deleted_at`), which is a wider shape than the one returned by `rules/list`.

- `orderby` accepts only `updated_at` or `version`; any other value (including omitted) falls back to `updated_at` rather than erroring.
- Results sort descending by default; pass `asc=true` for ascending order.

status.description: Status of the resource. A resource with status `deleted` or `destroyed` never reaches this field — the operation returns `ResourceNotFound` for those instead.

created_at.description: Unix timestamp in seconds when the resource was created. Also anchors the start of the first billing window.

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp in seconds when the resource was last updated.

window_start_time.description: Unix timestamp in seconds for the start of the current 30-day billing window.

window_end_time.description: Unix timestamp in seconds for the end of the current 30-day billing window.

session_limit_reached.description: `true` when a `version=free` account has exceeded its combined free session quota across all applications. Always `false` for non-free plans.

expired_at.description: Unix timestamp in seconds when the on-premises license expires. Only present on on-premises deployments; omitted entirely for SaaS accounts.

UpdateRemoteConfigRequest.description: Publish a whole new remote configuration version. The client sends the complete object, not a patch: rule order carries meaning.

application_id.description: RUM application ID.

reason.description: Operator's note on why this version was published. Stored verbatim.

UpdateRemoteConfigResponse.description: Version allocated to the published configuration.

items.description: Version items, newest first by default.

version.description: New version number created by the revert.

RemoteConfigValues.description: The SDK knobs a configuration can set. Every field is optional: a value absent from both rule and default is omitted from the SDK response, which tells the SDK to keep its init value.

traceSampleRate.description: Trace sampling rate (0-100): which sessions inject trace headers into their requests.

defaultPrivacyLevel.description: How Session Replay masks a page by default.

version.description: Version number, unique within the application.

content_hash.description: Hash of the configuration content; lets the console identify versions with identical content.

equivalent_to.description: Earliest version carrying the same content, when that is not this version itself.

reason.description: Operator's note left when the version was published. Empty when none was given.

updated_by.description: ID of the member who published the version.

updated_by_name.description: Name of the member who published the version.

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds - when the version was published.

PreviewRemoteConfigRequest.description: Preview request. Omit `config` to preview the currently live configuration.

application_id.description: RUM application ID.

app_version.description: App version the simulated client reports.

sdk.description: SDK name and version the simulated client reports, e.g. `web@2.4.1`.

RemoteConfigRule.description: One targeting rule: when `match` holds, `set` overrides `default`. The first matching rule wins and evaluation stops there - rule order is the priority.

match.description: Key/value conditions the SDK's config request must equal. Keys are limited to `env`, `app_version` and `sdk`; values are at most 256 bytes.

application_id.description: RUM application ID.

RemoteConfig.description: The whole per-application remote configuration. A change reaches an SDK asynchronously and is applied when that SDK creates its next session, so a running session never flips a decision mid-flight.

enabled.description: Kill switch. When false the engine reports no values at all and SDKs fall back to their init values.

activation.description: How a change lands on a client that is already running. Empty means `next_session`.

refresh_on_foreground.description: Let clients re-check the configuration when they return to the foreground instead of waiting for the next poll.

rules.description: Targeting rules, evaluated in order; at most 20 per application.

custom.description: Application-defined pass-through values handed to the host app verbatim. At most 5 keys, each key up to 64 bytes, each value up to 4 KB of JSON nested at most 3 levels, 16 KB in total. Anyone holding the public client token can read it.

RevertRemoteConfigRequest.description: Republish an earlier version's content under a new version number.

application_id.description: RUM application ID.

reason.description: Operator's note. The console fills in `rolled back to vN` when left empty.

PreviewRemoteConfigResponse.description: Values the simulated client would receive.

hit_rule_index.description: 0-based index of the rule that decided the result, or -1 when only the default applied.

GetRemoteConfigResponse.description: Live remote configuration and its version.

version.description: Version the live configuration is stored under. 0 means the application has never been configured.

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds - when the current version was published. 0 when never configured.

ListRemoteConfigHistoryRequest.description: Remote configuration history request. Newest first by default.

application_id.description: RUM application ID.

p.description: Zero-based page index; offset is p multiplied by limit.
